decisions.reason: Although it can broaden partnerships and knowledge inflows, an accelerator program is less tightly tied to our core machinery and recycling know-how, so our absorptive capacity is better used on technologies we can directly engineer, learn from, and scale commercially.

A bio-based CO2-negative bitumen binder is too far from our main knowledge base, customer set, and equipment capabilities, making it harder for our existing R&D to absorb lessons quickly and improve it efficiently.

An infectious waste decontamination plant is close to our established waste-treatment technology base and is supported by cooperation with partners, which fits our ability to assimilate external knowledge and refine the product.

A mobile mechanical recycling plant is highly aligned with our modular, decentralized recycling expertise and existing manufacturing capabilities, giving us strong capacity to interpret early market feedback and improve it further.
